style: Say evenly and clearly, like a calm, friendly college professor
lines: Welcome to Energy Accountant. Pick a scene, then press an entry. Every atom that goes in has to come out somewhere.
Oxygen switch. Set the work, press Tick, then switch the oxygen off and tick again.
Planet's books. Press a station button, then press Swing and look for the months the air loses carbon dioxide.
Where did the wood come from? Set the three sliders, then press Check.
Almost all of it came from the air. The carbon and most of the oxygen arrived as carbon dioxide.
Oxygen off. Each glucose now pays two ATP instead of about thirty two. Press Tick to see the cost.
Press Next stamp to follow one carbon atom through air, life, ocean and rock.
No light, so no photosynthesis. The leaf still respires. Press Respire to follow its stored sugar.
Press another entry, or pick a different scene. Watch the carbon bars change.
Choose Leaf by day and press Photosynthesize, or open Deer for its eaten-leaf stock.
Two glucose molecules join into sucrose and water; real cells pay for this with ATP. Pick another scene to compare.
Cells use many steps; this is an atom summary, not one real reaction. Nitrogen is counted as ammonia; pick another scene to compare.
Northern land plants draw down carbon dioxide in summer. Compare the station curves with Swing.
Your carbon has visited air, life, ocean and rock. Press Back to ledger to keep the books.
Keep Work fixed. Press Tick with oxygen on and off; compare glucose for the same ATP.
Pick a scene and press an entry. Every atom in must show up somewhere out.
Pick an entry. Every atom in must show up somewhere out.
Fermentation products stay in Body. Press another entry to compare where the atoms and energy go.
Plant nitrogen from soil nitrate is counted as ammonia. This is an atom summary, not one real reaction; pick another scene to compare.
Press an entry to start again. Each scene has its own opening stock.
Press Next stamp to follow your tagged carbon. Press Back to ledger to return.
Oxygen on. Press Tick to use about 32 ATP per glucose.
Press Tick to compare muscle with oxygen on and off. Earlier totals stay in their columns.
Press Tick to compare yeast with oxygen on and off. Earlier totals stay in their columns.
Press Swing to remove each baseline. Compare the months when each curve falls.
Press Swing to compare seasonal changes rather than raw concentrations.
Look for falling months and the lowest point. Press a station button to isolate its curve.
